subject: Post-call follow-up: SDK auth matrix, routing policy, embeddings/rerankers, ded. throughput questions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@fintrust.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + follow-up questions (SDK auth, routing, embeddings, dedicated sizing)

Alex / FinTrust team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope a dedicated proof-of-concept and long-lead artifacts. TL;DR: FinTrust wants private routing rules for risk-tiered traffic, token-level observability, an embeddings + reranker path for legal-search relevance, and a reserved GPU pool with burst capacity for month-end runs.

Notes from the call (short):
- Integration: plan to use Redwood SDK for service-to-service calls from FinTrust backend (Java).
- Auth: you’ll use your internal OIDC provider; asked about short-lived mTLS certs vs API keys for Dedicated.
- Routing: traffic split by risk tier (low/medium/high) with high going to a quantized large model in Dedicated, low to hosted smaller models.
- Embeddings: batch upsert to semantic store, then rerank top-k candidates with a lightweight cross-encoder.
- Capacity: estimated steady-state concurrency ~120 requests/min, peak bursts to 600 rpm during batch jobs.

Open technical questions we need answered to produce a sizing + integration plan: (can you reply inline?)
1) SDK & auth: Do you prefer OIDC token exchange (on-behalf-of) or issuing long-lived API keys scoped to the VPC for our Dedicated agent? Any constraints on outbound TLS cert pinning or proxying?
2) Routing & policy: Do you have a rule engine (e.g., Envoy/L7) that will classify risk tier, or do you want Redwood to accept a routing header and enforce it?
3) Structured output / tool-calling: For legal automation we expect to return JSON structured summaries and occasionally trigger a document-redaction tool. Will you want the Redwood structured-output feature (JSON schema + strict validation) enabled?
4) Embeddings/reranker: What's your expected embedding upsert cadence and index size (documents)? Rough ballpark will let us size GPU memory for vector batches.
5) Dedicated sizing: Confirm the 600 rpm peak is sustained or short bursts (seconds/minutes). Also, what latency SLO do you need for high-risk calls (p50/p95)?

Attachments: initial capacity workbook and a rough auth flow diagram attached — we’ll iterate once we get your answers.

Next steps (proposed):
- FinTrust to respond with answers to 1–5 above by EOD Thu (8/27).
- Redwood to produce a Dedicated sizing workbook + sample config and a short demo of structured-output in a sandbox.
- Schedule follow-up technical session (30–45m) to walk the config and finalize SLA targets.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet), auth-flow-diagram.png (image)
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@fintrust.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Eng <platform-eng@fintrust.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + follow-up questions (SDK auth, routing, embeddings, dedicated sizing)

Rishi — appreciate the clear notes. Replying inline below.

1) SDK & auth: We prefer short-lived OIDC tokens via our identity broker (on-behalf-of flow). Long-lived keys are a no-go for regulated PII flows. We do have a sidecar proxy for outbound, but it supports mTLS and will forward OIDC. No cert pinning on our side.

2) Routing & policy: We already tag traffic at the service layer with a header X-FT-RISK:{low,med,high}. Prefer Redwood to accept that header and enforce routing, rather than adding another rule engine.

3) Structured output/tool-calling: Yes — structured JSON responses would be ideal. For document redaction we’ll call an internal tool via webhook; would like Redwood to support action hooks that post to our webhook with a signed payload.

4) Embeddings/reranker: Expect ~250k documents initially, growing to ~1M over 12 months. Upserts will be nightly batches (1–2M embedding ops). Rerank after retrieval should operate on top-200 candidates.

5) Dedicated sizing: The 600 rpm figure is for month-end processing windows (~10–15 minutes). High-risk calls need 200ms p50 and 700ms p95 targets.

I’ve attached a short network/inbound policy PDF our infra team likes; cc’ing Platform Eng for any infra-level caveats. Happy to hop on a technical call Thursday afternoon.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTrust
attachments: fintrust-network-policy.pdf
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@fintrust.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + follow-up questions (SDK auth, routing, embeddings, dedicated sizing)

Alex — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. A few technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective so we scope correctly before the demo: 

- OIDC/on-behalf-of: we support OBO for Dedicated; we'll need the identity broker’s JWKS endpoint and a service account client ID so our private control plane can exchange tokens. Please send the URL and a test token if possible.

- Header-based routing: good — we can map X-FT-RISK to routing policies. We recommend enforcing a server-side allowlist for headers to prevent header spoofing (we can provide a signed header option if you want stronger guarantees).

- Embeddings: with 250k -> 1M documents and nightly batches we’ll size for 16–32GB vector batch memory and include a CPU preprocessor node. For rerank on top-200, suggest a dedicated CPU/GPU small cross-encoder pool — we’ll include that in the workbook.

- Concurrency and burst handling: for a 600 rpm 10–15 minute window, do you expect many concurrent long-context calls ( >512 tokens)? If yes, we’ll recommend reserved burst nodes with autoscale cooldowns. If mostly short (<=128 tokens), we can optimize for higher concurrency per GPU.

Action items for FinTrust before we finalize sizing:
1) Confirm JWKS URL + sample token OR indicate if you want to use mTLS for agent auth instead.
2) Confirm typical token lengths / average request token count for high-risk flows.
3) Indicate whether the reranker can accept top-200 candidate lists in a single request (preferred) or whether you need chunked scoring.

We’ll draft a Dedicated config draft and capacity workbook once we have 1–3. Proposing a follow-up 30m call Thursday 8/27 1pm PT — does that work?

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@fintrust.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + follow-up questions (SDK auth, routing, embeddings, dedicated sizing)

Alex — thanks for the quick answers yesterday. Attached is a first-pass Dedicated sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx) and a short proposal for the embeddings + reranker flow (embed-rerank-proposal.pdf). Highlights: 

- Base pool: 4x A100-equivalent nodes for steady traffic (aims to meet 120 rpm steady-state + 200ms p50 for high-risk).
- Burst pool: autoscale to +8 nodes for month-end windows (targets the 600 rpm short burst; autoscale cooldown 90s).
- Concurrency: we recommend per-GPU concurrency cap of 16 for long-context flows (>512 tokens) and 48 for short-context flows (<=128).
- Queuing: we’ll expose a priority queue (high/normal/low) tied to X-FT-RISK; high bypasses best-effort batching and gets reserved slots to meet p95.
- Auth: OBO tokens accepted; we’ll do a token-exchange flow with short-lived machine tokens to the agent.

Next steps:
- If FinTrust can share JWKS URL + sample token, we’ll finalize the agent auth exchange config and push a sandbox connector for you to validate.
- If the numbers look reasonable, we’ll schedule the Thursday 1pm PT call (already penciled) to walk the workbook and confirm SLA / pricing implications.

Would you like us to include an alternate plan that uses quantized model variants for low-risk traffic to reduce cost? We can surface the estimated cost delta in the workbook.

Thanks,
David Kim
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
